findings.claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T are honoured when present, and that contractless is only the fallback when T has no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject]. The collector never reads T's attributes. With no surrogate it always calls CreateContractlessMembers with string keys. A referenced type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] is therefore written as a name-keyed map instead of an int-keyed array, and [DataContract]/[DataMember(Order)] is ignored the same way. Ledger L19 says to follow the requirement here.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129AttributesHonouredTests.MessagePackObjectKeysOnReferencedTypeAreHonoured and DataContractOrderOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured. Each builds ProjectA with an attributed MyType and ProjectB with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class, serializes through the generated formatter, and expects JSON [5,"x"]. On head the output is a map {"Name":"x","Value":5}, so both tests fail.

findings.claim: GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute is read only by the source generator, including SurrogateType, which the docs say is read only at compile time. It is still declared without [Conditional("NEVERDEFINED")]. Ledger L14 records that generator-only attributes carry that marker on purpose so they are not emitted into user assemblies. Without it, every annotated formatter keeps the attribute and a typeof(surrogate) reference in metadata.

receipt_plan.detail: Cite L14. Compare the declaration with GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute and the other generator-only attributes in MessagePack.Annotations. Then compile a ProjectB using [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType=...)] and check that the formatter type's CustomAttributes in the emitted assembly still contain the attribute.
